files.detail: Replaced `beforeRegisterNodeDef` + `onNodeCreated` prototype chaining with `comfy.defs.extend('FastPreview', …)`. The two `api.addEventListener` preview subscriptions, the module-level `execId` written from the `executing` event, the `serverSupportsFeature('supports_preview_metadata')` probe and the `displayNodeId === this.id` test all collapse into `b.onPreview`, which delivers frames already correlated to the node — so `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener` are obsolete, not dropped. `node.imgs = [img]` + `setDirtyCanvas` become a `widgets.canvas` draw plus `redraw()`, which renders under both renderers. Per-node state is a Map keyed by `node.id`, cleared in `b.onRemoved`.
files.test:
equivalence — a FastPreview node still ends up 550x550 on creation, and a
preview frame addressed to that node still results in exactly one image being
displayed on the node (one image object retained per node, replaced on each
new frame). Loading the extension registers behaviour for the type
'FastPreview' and for no other type. Removing the node releases the per-node
preview state so no listener or image is retained. All of this holds on the
original source and on the converted source.

fix — with TWO FastPreview nodes previewing during the same run on a server
that does NOT report supports_preview_metadata, emit a plain `b_preview`
event while `executing` last named node A. On the ORIGINAL source both nodes'
plainHandler compare the single module-level `execId` against their own id,
so the frame is attributed by a global that is shared between them: node B
shows nothing while node A shows the frame, and if `executing` has already
advanced to B when A's frame arrives late, A's frame is shown on B —
mis-attribution. Asserting "each node only ever displays frames the backend
produced for it" FAILS on the original. On the CONVERTED source there is no
module-level `execId`: `onPreview` delivers each frame already correlated to
its own node handle, so the assertion PASSES.

Second fix claim: the original writes `node.imgs = [img]` and calls
`setDirtyCanvas`, which renders only under the legacy canvas renderer. Under
Nodes 2.0 the original displays nothing; the converted source draws through
`widgets.canvas`, which renders under both. Asserting "the preview is visible
with the legacy renderer disabled" fails before and passes after.

wire format — neither source adds, removes or reorders widgets that
serialize: the mounted canvas widget carries no value, and no widget value or
link is touched, so `graphToPrompt` output and the serialized workflow are
byte-identical between the two sources.

files.test:
PlaySoundKJ — audio playback on execution.

## Equivalence (must pass against BOTH the shipped file and the draft)

Setup: one PlaySoundKJ node with widgets mode/volume/duration. Stub `Audio`
(record constructor url, `volume`, `play()`, `pause()`) and stub `api.apiURL`
to return its argument. Deliver backend output by whichever route the source
uses — `nodeType.prototype.onExecuted(output)` for the shipped file,
`b.onExecuted(node, result)` with `result.raw === output` for the draft.

1. Empty / missing audio is a no-op.
   output `{}` and `{ audio: [] }` → no `Audio` is constructed.

2. mode "always" plays immediately at the widget volume.
   mode="always", volume=0.3, duration=0,
   output `{ audio: [{ filename: "a.flac", subfolder: "sub", type: "temp" }] }`
   → exactly one `Audio` constructed, url is
   `/view?filename=a.flac&subfolder=sub&type=temp`, `volume === 0.3`,
   `play()` called once, and no timer is scheduled.

3. Missing filename/subfolder/type default to "", "" and "temp".
   output `{ audio: [{}] }` → url `/view?filename=&subfolder=&type=temp`.

4. Missing widgets fall back to mode "always", volume 0.5, duration 0.
   Node with no widgets at all → one `Audio`, `volume === 0.5`, `play()` called.

5. volume is clamped to [0,1]: volume=5 → `volume === 1`; volume=-2 → `volume === 0`.

6. duration > 0 pauses the audio after duration seconds.
   duration=2 → advance fake timers 1999ms: `pause()` not called; advance past
   2000ms: `pause()` called exactly once.

7. mode "on_change" suppresses a repeat with the same hash.
   Execute twice with `{ audio: [...], audio_hash: ["h1"] }` → one `Audio` total.
   Execute a third time with `audio_hash: ["h2"]` → a second `Audio`.
   A null/absent `audio_hash` never suppresses: two executions with no
   `audio_hash` produce two `Audio` objects.

8. mode "on_empty_queue" defers until the queue drains, with a 1s debounce.
   Execute → no `Audio` yet, and a "status" listener is registered on `api`.
   Emit status `{ detail: { exec_info: { queue_remaining: 2 } } }` → still none.
   Emit `queue_remaining: 0`, advance 999ms → still none.
   Advance past 1000ms → one `Audio`, `play()` called, and the "status"
   listener has been removed from `api`.

9. A 0 that is followed by a non-zero inside the debounce window is cancelled.
   Emit `queue_remaining: 0`, advance 500ms, emit `queue_remaining: 1`,
   advance 5000ms → no `Audio` constructed and the listener is still registered.

10. Re-executing while a sound is playing stops the old one first.
    mode="always", duration=10, execute, then execute again → first audio's
    `pause()` called once, two `Audio` objects constructed, and only the second
    is still pending its stop timer (advance past 10s → second `pause()`).

11. Two PlaySoundKJ nodes keep independent state.
    Node A and node B both mode="on_change" with hash "h1": A executes (plays),
    B executes (plays — B has never seen "h1"). A executes again with "h1" → no
    third `Audio`. Two `Audio` objects total.

## Fix (expected to FAIL against the shipped file, pass against the draft)

Deleting the node while an "on_empty_queue" playback is pending must release
the subscription and not play.

  mode="on_empty_queue", execute → a "status" listener is registered.
  Now remove the node (`graph.remove(node)` for the shipped file;
  `b.onRemoved` fires for the draft).
  Expected: the "status" listener has been removed from `api`, and emitting
  `queue_remaining: 0` followed by advancing 5000ms constructs no `Audio`.

  The shipped file keeps its state on the node instance and never unsubscribes
  on removal, so the listener stays registered for the lifetime of the page and
  still fires playback for a node that no longer exists.

Also: deleting the node while a sound is playing must stop it.
  mode="always", duration=10, execute, remove the node → `pause()` called.
  The shipped file leaves the audio playing and the stop timer armed.

files.detail:
Four independent capabilities in the switch have no destination in v1/comfy-api.d.ts, and a partial conversion would leave prototype patching in the file.

1. Button widget callbacks (blocks 8 of the 14 cases). `this.addWidget("button", label, null, fn)` is used for "Update inputs" (setupDynamicInputs, driving ConditioningMultiCombine / ImageBatchMulti / ImageAddMulti / CrossFadeImagesMulti / TransitionImagesMulti / ImageConcatMulti / MaskBatchMulti / JoinStringMulti), "Set all" (FluxBlockLoraSelect / HunyuanVideoBlockLoraSelect / Wan21BlockLoraSelect / LTX2BlockLoraSelect) and "Start/Stop mic capture" (SoundReactive). `WidgetDef` has no callback/onClick field, and `WidgetHandle.on('change', ...)` cannot substitute: litegraph's ButtonWidget.onClick calls `this.callback?.(this.value, ...)`, so the bridged value equals the previous value and widgetHandle's `notify` early-returns. A button added via `node.widgets.add({ type: 'button', name: '...' })` is therefore inert. Needs either `WidgetDef.onClick` or an `on('click')` event.

2. `NodeHandle` has no `setTitle` — required by the PreviewAnimation case (`this.title = "Preview Animation " + values` in onExecuted, and the reset to "Preview Animation" on connect). `NodeSnapshot.title` is readonly; there is no writer anywhere on the handle.

3. No destination for a *computed* `widget.serializeValue`. SaveImageKJ / SaveImageWithAlpha / SaveStringKJ / DecodeAndSaveVideo / ModelSaveKJ / LoraExtractKJ set `widget.serializeValue = () => applyTextReplacements(app, widget.value)` on `filename_prefix`, so the value written into the prompt differs from the widget value (%date% etc. expanded). `WidgetDef.serialize` is a boolean and `WidgetHandle` exposes only `isSerialized()`; `b.onSerialize` returns extra keys, it cannot rewrite `widgets_values`. Dropping this is a wire-format change.

4. `widget.on('change', (value, oldValue))` loses the argument the pack branches on. setupDynamicInputs wraps `countW.callback = function (value, canvas) { ...; if (!canvas) rebuild(); }` — litegraph passes the canvas only for interactive edits, so the original deliberately rebuilds slots on API-format reload and NOT while the user scrubs the count. The change listener gets no such argument, so the converted version would reflow inputs on every keystroke. Real behaviour change, not cosmetic.

Minor, would have been droppable on their own: `slotOptions: {shape: 7}` (the hollow-circle optional-input marker) has no equivalent on `inputs.add(name, type)`; and `this.inputs_offset = ...` on ConditioningMultiCombine is an arbitrary node property (set here, never read anywhere in the pack).

Converted the `hideWidgetForGood` helper off the converted-widget protocol: the `computeSize = () => [0, -4]` hack and `widget.type = "converted-widget" + suffix` become `node.widgets.get(name).setHidden(true)`, so `type` is a rename onto `setHidden`, not lost behaviour. The `origType`/`origComputeSize`/`origSerializeValue` saves are deleted — grep confirms nothing in the pack ever read them back. The helper never installed a serializeValue suppressor, so hiding was already presentation-only and the wire format is unaffected. `node` is now a NodeHandle and the vestigial `suffix` parameter (it only mangled the type string) is gone; the helper has zero callers in the pack, so nothing is stranded. Every other export — notably `chainCallback`, which ~15 unconverted files still use — is untouched.
files.test:
equivalence — after `hideWidgetForGood(node, widget)` the named widget is not
drawn on the node, and every widget reachable through `widget.linkedWidgets`
(recursively) is also not drawn. The widget's *value* is unchanged, and the
set of widgets on the node is unchanged — nothing is added or removed. Every
other export of utility.js (`makeUUID`, `chainCallback`, `clientToCanvas`,
`getNodeAtPoint`, `typesCompatible`, `getSlotPos`, `addMiddleClickPan`,
`resolveSourcePreview`, `watchImageInputs`, `captureVideoFrame`,
`rectHitTest`, `cursorForBboxMode`, `addWheelPassthrough`) is untouched and
behaves identically; in particular `chainCallback`'s signature is unchanged,
which the ~15 unconverted files in this pack still depend on. Holds on the
original and on the converted source.

fix — hide a widget, then read back its type. On the ORIGINAL source
`widget.type` is now the string `"converted-widget"` (or
`"converted-widget:<parent>"` for a linked widget): the widget's *kind* has
been overwritten to express "hidden", so a subsequent `type`-based dispatch —
anything asking "is this a combo?" — no longer recognises it, and
`widget.computeSize()` returns the magic `[0, -4]` rather than the widget's
real size. Assert "hiding a widget leaves its type and computeSize
unchanged": FAILS on the original, PASSES on the converted source, where
hiding is `setHidden(true)` and type remains identity.

Second fix claim: the original stores `origType` / `origComputeSize` /
`origSerializeValue` on the widget and nothing in the pack ever reads them
back (grep confirms zero readers), so the widget is permanently mutated and
un-restorable. Assert "no `orig*` scratch fields are left on the widget":
fails before, passes after.

wire format — this helper never installed a `serializeValue` suppressor (it
saves `origSerializeValue` but never replaces `serializeValue`), so hiding was
already presentation-only on both sources: a hidden widget serialized before
and serializes after. `widgets_values` ordering, count and contents are
therefore identical, and `graphToPrompt` output and the serialized workflow
are byte-identical between the two sources.

files.detail: `nodeCreated` maps cleanly to `defs.extend([...], b => b.onCreated(...))` and `node.setSize({width,height})` exists, but the entire point of the file is node colouring: `node.color = ...` / `node.bgcolor = ...` for INTConstant, FloatConstant and ConditioningMultiCombine. `NodeHandle` exposes `color`/`bgColor` on `snapshot()` (read-only) and has NO `setColor`/`setBgColor` writer. It also reads `LGraphCanvas.node_colors.green` for the palette, which has no published equivalent. MISSING: `NodeHandle.setColor(color)` / `setBgColor(color)`, and a published accessor for the standard node-colour palette. Converting `setSize` alone would leave the prototype-free file doing nothing it was written to do.

Replaces the graph canvas's own background rendering: patches `canvas.onRenderBackground` and returns `true` to suppress LiteGraph's clear+grid, then fills the whole canvas with a repeat pattern built from `this.ds.scale`/`this.ds.offset`, `cvs.width/height` and `ctx.setTransform`. This is renderer-level painting on the shared graph context — the exact coupling `widgets.canvas` exists to end, and it has no per-node destination because it is not per node. Also depends on `app.ui.settings` (5 settings with onChange), `commands`, `menuCommands` and `app.canvas.setDirty`, none of which the published API exposes. Needs the author and a canvas-background capability in core, not a pack-level patch.

`chainCallback(nodeType.prototype, 'onNodeCreated')` → `b.onCreated` and `addDOMWidget('context_windows_viz', 'div', root, {serialize:false})` → `widgets.mount({name, render, destroy})` are both fine, but the node persists its own state as `node.properties.cw_viz = { step, steps }`, written during execution and read back in `onConfigure`. `NodeHandle` has no `getProperty`/`setProperty`, and `b.onSerialize` extras are merged at the top level of the serialized node rather than into `properties`, so moving the key there changes the saved workflow for every existing user file. MISSING: `NodeHandle.getProperty(key)` / `setProperty(key, value)`, or an `onSerialize` that can address the `properties` bag.

Two blockers. (1) The `getNodeMenuItems(node)` hook builds a menu for EVERY node type, not for types this pack owns; `b.addMenuItem` is per-definition, so there is no way to contribute an entry to all nodes. It also needs `has_submenu`/`submenu.options` for the Recreate-node submenu, which `NodeMenuItem {label, run}` cannot express. (2) `setup()` wraps `app.canvas.showConnectionMenu` and temporarily swaps `LiteGraph.ContextMenu` to splice 'Add SetNode'/'Add GetNode' in next to 'Add Reroute' — a SLOT connection menu, which the skill names as still a gap. Also uses `LiteGraph.createNode`, `graph.add`, `node.connect`, `findOutputSlot`, `app.canvas.selectNode`. MISSING: menu contribution to all node types, submenu support on `NodeMenuItem`, and any slot/canvas-menu surface.

Shared base class for the Points/Spline editors. Blocked on a stack of missing capabilities, not one: (a) `node.properties.imgData` read/write plus `node.addProperty(name, value, type)` for `points`/`neg_points` — no `getProperty`/`setProperty`/`addProperty` on `NodeHandle`; (b) `addDOMWidget(..., {getMinHeight, getMaxHeight, getHeight})` — `MountDef` takes a single fixed `height`, so a DOM widget whose height the pack recomputes has no destination; (c) `chainCallback(node, 'onResize')` to reflow the canvas on node resize — there is no `onResized` hook and `setSizeConstraints` cannot express "rescale my bitmap when the width changes"; (d) `node.pasteFile` / `node.onDragOver` / `node.onDragDrop` for image drag-and-drop — no published equivalent; (e) `node.arrange()`, `node.graph.setDirtyCanvas()`, `node.uuid`. MISSING: node property access, variable-height mounted widgets, a resize hook, and file drop/paste hooks.

Subclass of BaseEditorCanvas — inherits every gap in editors/editor_base.js (node properties, variable-height DOM widget, onResize, file drop) and cannot be converted while its base cannot. On top of that it drives everything through captured raw widget objects: `this.findWidget('coordinates')` then `widget.value = JSON.stringify(...)` and `widget.callback = () => ...` on `points_store`/`bbox_store`. Widget writes must go through `setValue`, and callback capture-and-chain through `on('change')`, but the base class hands it live widget objects rather than handles, so the two files must move together. Convert editor_base.js first.

Second subclass of BaseEditorCanvas, same blocker set — inherits the node-properties, variable-height-DOM-widget, `onResize` and drag-drop gaps from editors/editor_base.js and drives raw widget objects (`widget.value = ...`, `widget.callback = ...`) handed down by the base. Must be converted in the same change as editor_base.js and point_editor_canvas.js, once node property access and variable-height mounted widgets exist.

Everything else here converts — `onNodeCreated` → `b.onCreated`, `addDOMWidget` → `widgets.mount({render, destroy})` (the whole grid/detail/scrubber UI is already plain DOM with its own listeners, and the `ResizeObserver`/`keydown`/video teardown in `onRemoved` is exactly what `destroy` is for), `chainCallback(this,'onExecuted'|'onConfigure'|'onRemoved')` → `b.onExecuted`/`onConfigured`/`onRemoved`. The blocker is persistence: it stashes the backend's preview descriptor as `this.properties.kj_batch_preview = info` in `onExecuted` and reads it back in `onConfigure` so a reloaded workflow can re-fetch the strip. `NodeHandle` has no property access, and `b.onSerialize` extras land outside `properties`, so relocating the key would change every saved workflow that already contains it. MISSING: `NodeHandle.getProperty`/`setProperty`.

Pure editor tooling, hung entirely off registration surfaces the published API does not have: `settings` (fillConnectEnabled), `commands` (fillConnectSelected) and `keybindings` (`f` on graph-canvas). `graph.selection()` does replace `Object.values(canvas.selected_nodes)`, but the body then needs `LiteGraph.isValidConnection`, `node.connect(outIdx, target, inIdx)` across arbitrary nodes, `graph.getLink(linkId)`, `out.links` on foreign nodes, `node.pos`/`node.size` for the distance heuristic, `getSlotPos` (DOM slot positions) and `app.extensionManager.toast`. `OutputSlotHandle.connectTo` exists, but with no way to register the command or keybinding there is no entry point at all. MISSING: settings/commands/keybindings registration, and a toast/notification surface.

`fixNode(oldNode, comfyClass)` is a node-replacement routine: serialize the old node, `LiteGraph.createNode(comfyClass)`, `graph.add`, copy pos/size/title/color/bgcolor/flags/mode/properties, restore widget values by name, re-resolve every link through `app.graph.links[id]` and reconnect by slot name, then `graph.remove(oldNode)`. This is exactly `graph.replaceNode(id, newType, {widgets, keepPosition})`, which the spec describes but which is marked specified-only and is absent from the generated API — `GraphHandle` has `add`/`remove`/`node`/`nodes`/`links`/`selection` and nothing else. Rebuilding it by hand would need `snapshot()`-based cosmetics writers (`setTitle`, `setColor`, `setMode`, `setCollapsed`, properties) that also do not exist, and cross-node link re-homing, which `moveLinksTo` deliberately does not cover. MISSING: `graph.replaceNode`.

Three separate gaps. (1) `node.properties.hdrLastPreview = {...}` written in `onExecuted` and restored in `onConfigure` — no `getProperty`/`setProperty` on `NodeHandle` and `onSerialize` extras land outside `properties`. (2) `addDOMWidget('hdr_preview', ..., {getMinHeight/getHeight})` plus `chainCallback(node,'onResize')` to resize the canvas — `MountDef` takes a fixed `height` and there is no resize hook. (3) It sniffs other widgets with `if (w.hidden || w.type === 'converted-widget') continue` while measuring layout; `WidgetHandle` exposes `isHidden()`, but the surrounding manual layout arithmetic exists only because the pack is positioning its own DOM inside the node body. MISSING: node property access, variable-height mounted widgets, and a node-resize hook.

`addDocumentation` patches `nodeType.prototype.onDrawForeground` to paint a '?' glyph into the shared graph context at `this.size[0] - iconSize - iconMargin`, and pairs it with a patched `nodeType.prototype.onMouseDown` that hand-hit-tests `localPos` against those same coordinates to toggle the popup. It then positions the DOM popup by composing `ctx.getTransform()` with `canvas.getBoundingClientRect()` and `app.canvas.ds.scale` into a `DOMMatrix` on every repaint. That is a hand-painted interactive control whose behaviour depends on the canvas transform and draw order — the case the skill says needs the author. The file already ships a Nodes-2.0 path (a MutationObserver injecting a `.kj-help-btn` into `.lg-node-header`), which is the shape the converted version should keep, but choosing to delete the canvas path outright is the author's call, not a mechanical conversion.

2,701 lines / 157 KB — a whole floating dock-panel prompt builder. Beyond size it is blocked on the same constructs as the rest of the pack, in bulk: ~40 distinct `node.properties.*` keys (dockGraph, dockRect, dockPinned, dockMin, exposeToParent, guide, gridSize, snap, guideColor, guideOpacity, textSize, boxOpacity, liveBg, docked...) all persisted through the properties bag with no `getProperty`/`setProperty`; `chainCallback(app.canvas, 'onDrawForeground', ...)` used deliberately as a per-frame tick (`installDockWakes`, `sweepOrphanDocks`, `wakeDocks`) because nothing else notified it of graph change — the published answer is a change subscription, and `GraphHandle` has no `onChange`; and direct `app.canvas.ds.scale` reads to keep the panel aligned to the canvas. Needs the author, and needs node property access plus a graph change event before it can move.

2,058 lines / 97 KB — an interactive crop/rotate/transform editor. Same blocker profile as the rest of the pack, at scale: ~15 persisted `node.properties.*` keys (rotation, fillColor, gridSize, gridColor, previewEnabled, showRotationCross, canvasSize, previewFile) round-tripped through `onConfigure`, with no property access on `NodeHandle`; `node.onDrawForeground` patched on the INSTANCE (`const origDrawFg = node.onDrawForeground; node.onDrawForeground = ...`) rather than the prototype; `addDOMWidget('crop_preview', ...)` plus `chainCallback(this, 'onResize')` recomputing `node.properties.canvasSize` on every resize, which needs a resize hook and a variable-height mounted widget. Needs the author.

Drag-a-node-onto-a-link insertion, implemented entirely against the canvas: it iterates `graph.links` to hit-test the dragged node's bounding box against a hand-evaluated bezier (`bezierAt`, `bezierOffsetX` deliberately mirroring LiteGraph's own control-point maths so the hit region matches the drawn curve), sets LiteGraph's private `link._dragging` flag to hide the real link, and paints an animated dashed ghost link by chaining `lgCanvas.onDrawForeground` and drawing into the shared graph context with `LGraphCanvas.link_type_colors`. It also reads `lgCanvas.connecting_links`, `resizing_node`, `node_widget`, `selected_nodes`, `ds.scale` and drives a `requestAnimationFrame` loop off `setDirty`. Drawing between nodes on the graph canvas has no destination — `widgets.canvas` is per node — and the whole feature depends on canvas draw order and internal drag state. Needs the author.

Hold-a-key-and-drag to swap two nodes. Paints a pulsing glow outline around the target node by patching `lgCanvas.onDrawBackground` and stroking a `roundRect` at `target.pos`/`target.size` in the shared graph context — an overlay around a node, which `widgets.canvas` (a widget inside one node) cannot express. Detects the target with `getOverlappingNode` walking `graph._nodes` in reverse render order, and animates the swap either by mutating `node.pos` per frame or, in Vue mode, by writing a CSS transition onto `document.querySelector('[data-node-id]')`. Link surgery uses `disconnectAll` + `snapshotConnections` over `inp.link` / `out.links` and reconnects by name/type — that part has handles, but it is inseparable from the canvas overlay and the `LiteGraph.vueNodesMode` branch. Needs the author.

A renderer tuning panel. It monkey-patches `LGraphCanvas` methods on the live canvas — swaps `canvas.draw` to alias `bgcanvas`/`bgctx` onto the foreground canvas during `dragging_canvas`, and swaps `canvas.renderInfo` to blit a throttled offscreen cache — and writes `canvas.render_shadows`, `canvas.render_connections_border` and the global `LiteGraph.ROUND_RADIUS`. Every one of these is an internal of the renderer this programme is replacing; none has, or should have, a published destination. It is also driven by `settings`/`commands`/`menuCommands` registration, which the API does not expose. This file becomes obsolete under Nodes 2.0 rather than converted.

948 lines. `onNodeCreated` → `b.onCreated`, `addDOMWidget('preview','kj_preview',root,{serialize:false})` → `widgets.mount`, and the `onRemoved` teardown (a document-level `keydown` listener) → `destroy` are all straightforward. The blocker is `node.properties.kjPovPanelH`, the user's resized panel height, written on resize and read back in `onConfigure` to restore it — `NodeHandle` has no `getProperty`/`setProperty`, and `b.onSerialize` extras are merged outside `properties`, so relocating the key changes every already-saved workflow. MISSING: `NodeHandle.getProperty`/`setProperty`.

Screen-capture node. Two hard blockers. (1) `frameWidget.serializeValue = () => serializeCanvas.toDataURL('image/png')` — a COMPUTED serialize value that captures the current video frame at prompt time. `WidgetDef.serialize` is a boolean only; there is no transform hook, and dropping it means the node sends no frame at all. (2) `btnWidget = this.addWidget('button', 'Start capture', null, async () => {...})` and a second 'Hide preview' button — `widgets.add({type:'button'})` has no callback field, so the button would render inert (a `WidgetDef` carries value/options/disabled/hidden/serialize and nothing invokable). Also `frameWidget.computeSize = () => [0,-4]` (→ `setHidden`, fine), `btnWidget.name = '🔴 0:05 - Stop capture'` mutating a widget's NAME to show an elapsed timer (`setLabel` changes the label, not the name — check whether that is equivalent here), and `cropWWidget.options.max = video.videoWidth` (→ `setOption`, fine). MISSING: a computed/transforming serialize hook, and a button-widget callback.

1,711 lines — the SetNode/GetNode pair, the pack's flagship feature, and the single largest conversion in it. `class SetNode extends LGraphNode` / `class GetNode extends LGraphNode` + `LiteGraph.registerNodeType` + `isVirtualNode` maps in principle to `defs.define({type, execution:'frontend', resolve})` with a `forwardTo` resolver (Get → Set → source), which is exactly the case `resolution.ts` was designed for. What blocks it: (a) `this.properties.previousName` — the rename-tracking state both classes depend on — has no property access on `NodeHandle`, and it is part of the serialized node; (b) `getExtraMenuOptions(_, options)` on both classes needs submenu entries and 'go to node' navigation that `NodeMenuItem {label, run}` cannot express; (c) `LGraphCanvas.prototype.computeVisibleNodes` is patched at line 1370 to keep Get/Set nodes visible — a renderer internal with no destination; (d) `Object.values(app.canvas.selected_nodes)` in four places (→ `graph.selection()`, fine) alongside direct `output.links` / `input.link` link-walking to find the upstream Set node. The flagged `widgets.splice(idx,1); splice(idx,0,w)` at lines 999-1000 is NOT a reorder — it is cache invalidation after `w.options = newOpts`, and it converts to `widget.setOption('values', ...)`, which must use the descriptor-preserving `setOption` because the pack builds `values` as a live getter via `Object.defineProperty`. That one is solved; the four above are not. Best handled as an upstream PR with Kijai. MISSING: node property access, richer node menu items, and a supported way to influence node visibility.

Shake-a-node-to-drop-its-links gesture. The trigger is a document-level `pointermove` loop measuring direction reversals of `node.pos` scaled by `lgCanvas.ds.scale`, gated on `lgCanvas.connecting_links` / `resizing_node` / `node_widget` and reading the drag selection from `lgCanvas.selectedItems` — canvas drag state with no published equivalent (`graph.selection()` gives the selection but not the fact that a drag is in progress, nor per-frame positions). The link surgery underneath is expressible (`inp.link`/`out.links` walking → `input.link()`/`output.links()`, `disconnectInput` → `input.disconnect()`), and the bypass pass could use `connectTo`, but it is wrapped in `emitBeforeChange`/`beforeChange`/`afterChange` undo bracketing that also has no destination. A gesture defined by canvas pointer mechanics needs the author. MISSING (secondary): an undo-batching primitive such as `graph.batch(fn)`.

skillNotes.claim: A `button` widget cannot be converted: `WidgetDef` has no callback field and `widget.on('change')` never fires for one, because litegraph's `ButtonWidget.onClick` calls `this.callback?.(this.value, ...)` and the handle's change bridge early-returns when `value === previous` — so `addWidget("button", label, null, fn)` is an api-gap, not a `widgets.add({ type: 'button' })`.
skillNotes.evidence: kjnodes jsnodes.js uses `this.addWidget("button", "Update inputs", null, rebuild)`, `"Set all"`, and `"Start/Stop mic capture"`; src/lib/litegraph/src/widgets/ButtonWidget.ts:69 is `this.callback?.(this.value, canvas, node, pos, e)`, and widgetHandle's `notify` is `if (value === previous) return`.

skillNotes.claim: Before converting a `widget.callback` capture-and-chain to `on('change', ...)`, check whether the pack reads the callback's *second* argument — litegraph passes the canvas only for interactive edits, so `if (!canvas)` means "API-format reload, not a user scrub", and the change listener's `(value, oldValue)` signature cannot express that distinction.
skillNotes.evidence: kjnodes jsnodes.js `setupDynamicInputs`: `countW.callback = function (value, canvas) { ...; if (!canvas) rebuild(); }` — rebuilding on every interactive edit instead would reflow the node's input slots while the user drags the count widget.

skillNotes.claim: `NodeHandle` has no title writer — `NodeSnapshot.title` is readonly and there is no `setTitle` — so any `this.title = ...` used as a live readout (size, progress, frame count) is an api-gap, not a `setTitle` rename.
skillNotes.evidence: kjnodes jsnodes.js PreviewAnimation case sets `this.title = "Preview Animation " + values` inside onExecuted and resets it in onConnectInput; v1/comfy-api.d.ts NodeHandle declares getPosition/setPosition/getSize/setSize but no title accessor.

skillNotes.claim: `WidgetDef.serialize` is a boolean, so a *computed* `widget.serializeValue = () => transform(widget.value)` (the `applyTextReplacements` on `filename_prefix` idiom, present in dozens of save-node packs) has no destination — `onSerialize` adds keys alongside the node, it cannot rewrite `widgets_values`, and dropping the transform is a wire-format change.
